standard_prerequisites.name: Fibral definition of at-worst-nodal morphisms
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same unit, the definition of at-worst-nodal morphisms of relative dimension 1
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof reduces to the fibres because the at-worst-nodal condition on a flat locally finitely presented morphism is a condition on its fibres, by definition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nodal and smooth points under separable extension
standard_prerequisites.use: The nodal case of the fibre statement follows from Lemma lemma-node-over-separable-extension; the smooth-point case is the standard stability of smoothness under field extension.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 5017-5023): if S' -> S is etale and f : X -> S' is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension 1, then the composition g : X -> S is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension 1.

Flatness and finite presentation (proof lines 5025-5031): g is flat and locally of finite presentation as a composition of such morphisms, by the standard Morphisms lemmas on etale morphisms and composition.
Fibre reduction (line 5031-5033): hence it suffices to prove the fibres of g have at-worst-nodal singularities, which is exactly what the definition asks for.

Fibre cases (lines 5033-5037): the fibre over a point of S is the base change of a fibre of f by a separable field extension, so the nodal points are covered by Lemma lemma-node-over-separable-extension and the smooth points by the standard stability of smoothness under field extension.
proof_roadmap: Check flatness and local finite presentation by composition.
Reduce to fibres by the fibral nature of the definition.
Handle nodal and smooth points of the fibre under the separable base change.
difficulty_reason: Stability lemma (statement 5017-5023, proof 5025-5037): postcomposing an at-worst-nodal morphism by an etale morphism stays at-worst-nodal - the proof combines the standard composition lemmas for flatness and finite presentation with the fibral nature of the definition and the two fibre cases; the smooth-point case is the standard base-change stability of smoothness and is stated without a marker; no step is omitted. H2: short stability argument.
